text: demonstrate phonological awareness by: (i) identifying and producing rhyming words; (ii) recognizing spoken alliteration or groups of words that begin with the same spoken onset or initial sound; (iii) identifying the individual words in a spoken sentence; (iv) identifying syllables in spoken words; (v) blending syllables to form multisyllabic words; (vi) segmenting multisyllabic words into syllables; (vii) blending spoken onsets and rimes to form simple words; (viii) blending spoken phonemes to form one-syllable words; (ix) manipulating syllables within a multisyllabic word; and (x) segmenting spoken one-syllable words into individual phonemes;

strand_text: Inquiry and research: listening, speaking, reading, writing, and thinking using multiple texts. The student engages in both short-term and sustained recursive inquiry processes for a variety of purposes. The student is expected to:
text: use an appropriate mode of delivery, whether written, oral, or multimodal, to present results.

subject: MATH
strand_text: Mathematical process standards. The student uses mathematical processes to acquire and demonstrate mathematical understanding. The student is expected to:
text: apply mathematics to problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Mathematical process standards. The student uses mathematical processes to acquire and demonstrate mathematical understanding. The student is expected to:
text: use a problem-solving model that incorporates analyzing given information, formulating a plan or strategy, determining a solution, justifying the solution, and evaluating the problem-solving process and the reasonableness of the solution;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Mathematical process standards. The student uses mathematical processes to acquire and demonstrate mathematical understanding. The student is expected to:
text: select tools, including real objects, manipulatives, paper and pencil, and technology as appropriate, and techniques, including mental math, estimation, and number sense as appropriate, to solve problems;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Mathematical process standards. The student uses mathematical processes to acquire and demonstrate mathematical understanding. The student is expected to:
text: communicate mathematical ideas, reasoning, and their implications using multiple representations, including symbols, diagrams, graphs, and language as appropriate;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Mathematical process standards. The student uses mathematical processes to acquire and demonstrate mathematical understanding. The student is expected to:
text: create and use representations to organize, record, and communicate mathematical ideas;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Mathematical process standards. The student uses mathematical processes to acquire and demonstrate mathematical understanding. The student is expected to:
text: analyze mathematical relationships to connect and communicate mathematical ideas; and

subject: MATH
strand_text: Mathematical process standards. The student uses mathematical processes to acquire and demonstrate mathematical understanding. The student is expected to:
text: display, explain, and justify mathematical ideas and arguments using precise mathematical language in written or oral communication.

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to represent, compare, and order whole numbers and decimals and understand relationships related to place value. The student is expected to:
text: interpret the value of each place-value position as 10 times the position to the right and as one-tenth of the value of the place to its left;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to represent, compare, and order whole numbers and decimals and understand relationships related to place value. The student is expected to:
text: represent the value of the digit in whole numbers through 1,000,000,000 and decimals to the hundredths using expanded notation and numerals;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to represent, compare, and order whole numbers and decimals and understand relationships related to place value. The student is expected to:
text: compare and order whole numbers to 1,000,000,000 and represent comparisons using the symbols >, <, or =;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to represent, compare, and order whole numbers and decimals and understand relationships related to place value. The student is expected to:
text: round whole numbers to a given place value through the hundred thousands place;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to represent, compare, and order whole numbers and decimals and understand relationships related to place value. The student is expected to:
text: represent decimals, including tenths and hundredths, using concrete and visual models and money;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to represent, compare, and order whole numbers and decimals and understand relationships related to place value. The student is expected to:
text: compare and order decimals using concrete and visual models to the hundredths;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to represent, compare, and order whole numbers and decimals and understand relationships related to place value. The student is expected to:
text: relate decimals to fractions that name tenths and hundredths; and

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to represent, compare, and order whole numbers and decimals and understand relationships related to place value. The student is expected to:
text: determine the corresponding decimal to the tenths or hundredths place of a specified point on a number line.

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to represent and generate fractions to solve problems. The student is expected to:
text: represent a fraction a/b as a sum of fractions 1/b, where a and b are whole numbers and b > 0, including when a > b;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to represent and generate fractions to solve problems. The student is expected to:
text: decompose a fraction in more than one way into a sum of fractions with the same denominator using concrete and pictorial models and recording results with symbolic representations;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to represent and generate fractions to solve problems. The student is expected to:
text: determine if two given fractions are equivalent using a variety of methods;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to represent and generate fractions to solve problems. The student is expected to:
text: compare two fractions with different numerators and different denominators and represent the comparison using the symbols >, =, or <;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to represent and generate fractions to solve problems. The student is expected to:
text: represent and solve addition and subtraction of fractions with equal denominators using objects and pictorial models that build to the number line and properties of operations;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to represent and generate fractions to solve problems. The student is expected to:
text: evaluate the reasonableness of sums and differences of fractions using benchmark fractions 0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, and 1, referring to the same whole; and

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to represent and generate fractions to solve problems. The student is expected to:
text: represent fractions and decimals to the tenths or hundredths as distances from zero on a number line.

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to develop and use strategies and methods for whole number computations and decimal sums and differences in order to solve problems with efficiency and accuracy. The student is expected to:
text: add and subtract whole numbers and decimals to the hundredths place using the standard algorithm;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to develop and use strategies and methods for whole number computations and decimal sums and differences in order to solve problems with efficiency and accuracy. The student is expected to:
text: determine products of a number and 10 or 100 using properties of operations and place value understandings;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to develop and use strategies and methods for whole number computations and decimal sums and differences in order to solve problems with efficiency and accuracy. The student is expected to:
text: represent the product of 2 two-digit numbers using arrays, area models, or equations, including perfect squares through 15 by 15;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to develop and use strategies and methods for whole number computations and decimal sums and differences in order to solve problems with efficiency and accuracy. The student is expected to:
text: use strategies and algorithms, including the standard algorithm, to multiply up to a four-digit number by a one-digit number and to multiply a two-digit number by a two-digit number. Strategies may include mental math, partial products, and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to develop and use strategies and methods for whole number computations and decimal sums and differences in order to solve problems with efficiency and accuracy. The student is expected to:
text: represent the quotient of up to a four-digit whole number divided by a one-digit whole number using arrays, area models, or equations;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to develop and use strategies and methods for whole number computations and decimal sums and differences in order to solve problems with efficiency and accuracy. The student is expected to:
text: use strategies and algorithms, including the standard algorithm, to divide up to a four-digit dividend by a one-digit divisor;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to develop and use strategies and methods for whole number computations and decimal sums and differences in order to solve problems with efficiency and accuracy. The student is expected to:
text: round to the nearest 10, 100, or 1,000 or use compatible numbers to estimate solutions involving whole numbers; and

subject: MATH
strand_text: Number and operations. The student applies mathematical process standards to develop and use strategies and methods for whole number computations and decimal sums and differences in order to solve problems with efficiency and accuracy. The student is expected to:
text: solve with fluency one- and two-step problems involving multiplication and division, including interpreting remainders.

subject: MATH
strand_text: Algebraic reasoning. The student applies mathematical process standards to develop concepts of expressions and equations. The student is expected to:
text: represent multi-step problems involving the four operations with whole numbers using strip diagrams and equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Algebraic reasoning. The student applies mathematical process standards to develop concepts of expressions and equations. The student is expected to:
text: represent problems using an input-output table and numerical expressions to generate a number pattern that follows a given rule representing the relationship of the values in the resulting sequence and their position in the sequence;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Algebraic reasoning. The student applies mathematical process standards to develop concepts of expressions and equations. The student is expected to:
text: use models to determine the formulas for the perimeter of a rectangle (l + w + l + w or 2l + 2w), including the special form for perimeter of a square (4s) and the area of a rectangle (l x w); and

subject: MATH
strand_text: Algebraic reasoning. The student applies mathematical process standards to develop concepts of expressions and equations. The student is expected to:
text: solve problems related to perimeter and area of rectangles where dimensions are whole numbers.

subject: MATH
strand_text: Geometry and measurement. The student applies mathematical process standards to analyze geometric attributes in order to develop generalizations about their properties. The student is expected to:
text: identify points, lines, line segments, rays, angles, and perpendicular and parallel lines;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Geometry and measurement. The student applies mathematical process standards to analyze geometric attributes in order to develop generalizations about their properties. The student is expected to:
text: identify and draw one or more lines of symmetry, if they exist, for a two-dimensional figure;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Geometry and measurement. The student applies mathematical process standards to analyze geometric attributes in order to develop generalizations about their properties. The student is expected to:
text: apply knowledge of right angles to identify acute, right, and obtuse triangles; and

subject: MATH
strand_text: Geometry and measurement. The student applies mathematical process standards to analyze geometric attributes in order to develop generalizations about their properties. The student is expected to:
text: classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines or the presence or absence of angles of a specified size.

subject: MATH
strand_text: Geometry and measurement. The student applies mathematical process standards to solve problems involving angles less than or equal to 180 degrees. The student is expected to:
text: illustrate the measure of an angle as the part of a circle whose center is at the vertex of the angle that is "cut out" by the rays of the angle. Angle measures are limited to whole numbers;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Geometry and measurement. The student applies mathematical process standards to solve problems involving angles less than or equal to 180 degrees. The student is expected to:
text: illustrate degrees as the units used to measure an angle, where 1/360 of any circle is one degree and an angle that "cuts" n/360 out of any circle whose center is at the angle's vertex has a measure of n degrees. Angle measures are limited to whole numbers;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Geometry and measurement. The student applies mathematical process standards to solve problems involving angles less than or equal to 180 degrees. The student is expected to:
text: determine the approximate measures of angles in degrees to the nearest whole number using a protractor;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Geometry and measurement. The student applies mathematical process standards to solve problems involving angles less than or equal to 180 degrees. The student is expected to:
text: draw an angle with a given measure; and

subject: MATH
strand_text: Geometry and measurement. The student applies mathematical process standards to solve problems involving angles less than or equal to 180 degrees. The student is expected to:
text: determine the measure of an unknown angle formed by two non-overlapping adjacent angles given one or both angle measures.

subject: MATH
strand_text: Geometry and measurement. The student applies mathematical process standards to select appropriate customary and metric units, strategies, and tools to solve problems involving measurement. The student is expected to:
text: identify relative sizes of measurement units within the customary and metric systems;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Geometry and measurement. The student applies mathematical process standards to select appropriate customary and metric units, strategies, and tools to solve problems involving measurement. The student is expected to:
text: convert measurements within the same measurement system, customary or metric, from a smaller unit into a larger unit or a larger unit into a smaller unit when given other equivalent measures represented in a table; and

subject: MATH
strand_text: Geometry and measurement. The student applies mathematical process standards to select appropriate customary and metric units, strategies, and tools to solve problems involving measurement. The student is expected to:
text: solve problems that deal with measurements of length, intervals of time, liquid volumes, mass, and money using addition, subtraction, multiplication, or division as appropriate..

subject: MATH
strand_text: Data analysis. The student applies mathematical process standards to solve problems by collecting, organizing, displaying, and interpreting data. The student is expected to:
text: represent data on a frequency table, dot plot, or stem-and-leaf plot marked with whole numbers and fractions; and

subject: MATH
strand_text: Data analysis. The student applies mathematical process standards to solve problems by collecting, organizing, displaying, and interpreting data. The student is expected to:
text: solve one- and two-step problems using data in whole number, decimal, and fraction form in a frequency table, dot plot, or stem-and-leaf plot.

subject: MATH
strand_text: Personal financial literacy. The student applies mathematical process standards to manage one's financial resources effectively for lifetime financial security. The student is expected to:
text: distinguish between fixed and variable expenses;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Personal financial literacy. The student applies mathematical process standards to manage one's financial resources effectively for lifetime financial security. The student is expected to:
text: calculate profit in a given situation;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Personal financial literacy. The student applies mathematical process standards to manage one's financial resources effectively for lifetime financial security. The student is expected to:
text: compare the advantages and disadvantages of various savings options;

subject: MATH
strand_text: Personal financial literacy. The student applies mathematical process standards to manage one's financial resources effectively for lifetime financial security. The student is expected to:
text: describe how to allocate a weekly allowance among spending; saving, including for college; and sharing; and

subject: MATH
strand_text: Personal financial literacy. The student applies mathematical process standards to manage one's financial resources effectively for lifetime financial security. The student is expected to:
text: describe the basic purpose of financial institutions, including keeping money safe, borrowing money, and lending.

subject: SCI
strand_text: Scientific and engineering practices. The student asks questions, identifies problems, and plans and safely conducts classroom, laboratory, and field investigations to answer questions, explain phenomena, or design solutions using appropriate tools and models. The student is expected to:
text: ask questions and define problems based on observations or information from text, phenomena, models, or investigations;

subject: SCI
strand_text: Scientific and engineering practices. The student asks questions, identifies problems, and plans and safely conducts classroom, laboratory, and field investigations to answer questions, explain phenomena, or design solutions using appropriate tools and models. The student is expected to:
text: use scientific practices to plan and conduct descriptive investigations and use engineering practices to design solutions to problems;

subject: SCI
strand_text: Scientific and engineering practices. The student asks questions, identifies problems, and plans and safely conducts classroom, laboratory, and field investigations to answer questions, explain phenomena, or design solutions using appropriate tools and models. The student is expected to:
text: demonstrate safe practices and the use of safety equipment during classroom and field investigations as outlined in Texas Education Agency-approved safety standards;

subject: SCI
strand_text: Scientific and engineering practices. The student asks questions, identifies problems, and plans and safely conducts classroom, laboratory, and field investigations to answer questions, explain phenomena, or design solutions using appropriate tools and models. The student is expected to:
text: use tools, including hand lenses; metric rulers; Celsius thermometers; calculators; laser pointers; mirrors; digital scales; balances; graduated cylinders; beakers; hot plates; meter sticks; magnets; notebooks; timing devices; sieves; materials for building circuits; materials to support observation of habitats of organisms such as terrariums, aquariums, and collecting nets; and materials to support digital data collection such as computers, tablets, and cameras, to observe, measure, test, and analyze information;

subject: SCI
strand_text: Scientific and engineering practices. The student asks questions, identifies problems, and plans and safely conducts classroom, laboratory, and field investigations to answer questions, explain phenomena, or design solutions using appropriate tools and models. The student is expected to:
text: collect observations and measurements as evidence;

subject: SCI
strand_text: Scientific and engineering practices. The student asks questions, identifies problems, and plans and safely conducts classroom, laboratory, and field investigations to answer questions, explain phenomena, or design solutions using appropriate tools and models. The student is expected to:
text: construct appropriate graphic organizers used to collect data, including tables, bar graphs, line graphs, tree maps, concept maps, Venn diagrams, flow charts or sequence maps, and input-output tables that show cause and effect; and

subject: SCI
strand_text: Scientific and engineering practices. The student asks questions, identifies problems, and plans and safely conducts classroom, laboratory, and field investigations to answer questions, explain phenomena, or design solutions using appropriate tools and models. The student is expected to:
text: develop and use models to represent phenomena, objects, and processes or design a prototype for a solution to a problem.

subject: SCI
strand_text: Scientific and engineering practices. The student analyzes and interprets data to derive meaning, identify features and patterns, and discover relationships or correlations to develop evidence-based arguments or evaluate designs. The student is expected to:
text: identify advantages and limitations of models such as their size, scale, properties, and materials;

subject: SCI
strand_text: Scientific and engineering practices. The student analyzes and interprets data to derive meaning, identify features and patterns, and discover relationships or correlations to develop evidence-based arguments or evaluate designs. The student is expected to:
text: analyze data by identifying any significant features, patterns, or sources of error;

subject: SCI
strand_text: Scientific and engineering practices. The student analyzes and interprets data to derive meaning, identify features and patterns, and discover relationships or correlations to develop evidence-based arguments or evaluate designs. The student is expected to:
text: use mathematical calculations to compare patterns and relationships; and

subject: SCI
strand_text: Scientific and engineering practices. The student analyzes and interprets data to derive meaning, identify features and patterns, and discover relationships or correlations to develop evidence-based arguments or evaluate designs. The student is expected to:
text: evaluate a design or object using criteria.

subject: SCI
strand_text: Scientific and engineering practices. The student develops evidence-based explanations and communicates findings, conclusions, and proposed solutions. The student is expected to:
text: develop explanations and propose solutions supported by data and models;

subject: SCI
strand_text: Scientific and engineering practices. The student develops evidence-based explanations and communicates findings, conclusions, and proposed solutions. The student is expected to:
text: communicate explanations and solutions individually and collaboratively in a variety of settings and formats; and

subject: SCI
strand_text: Scientific and engineering practices. The student develops evidence-based explanations and communicates findings, conclusions, and proposed solutions. The student is expected to:
text: listen actively to others' explanations to identify relevant evidence and engage respectfully in scientific discussion.

subject: SCI
strand_text: Scientific and engineering practices. The student knows the contributions of scientists and recognizes the importance of scientific research and innovation for society. The student is expected to:
text: explain how scientific discoveries and innovative solutions to problems impact science and society; and

subject: SCI
strand_text: Scientific and engineering practices. The student knows the contributions of scientists and recognizes the importance of scientific research and innovation for society. The student is expected to:
text: research and explore resources such as museums, libraries, professional organizations, private companies, online platforms, and mentors employed in a science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) field to investigate STEM careers.

subject: SCI
strand_text: Recurring themes and concepts. The student understands that recurring themes and concepts provide a framework for making connections across disciplines. The student is expected to:
text: identify and use patterns to explain scientific phenomena or to design solutions;

subject: SCI
strand_text: Recurring themes and concepts. The student understands that recurring themes and concepts provide a framework for making connections across disciplines. The student is expected to:
text: identify and investigate cause-and-effect relationships to explain scientific phenomena or analyze problems;

subject: SCI
strand_text: Recurring themes and concepts. The student understands that recurring themes and concepts provide a framework for making connections across disciplines. The student is expected to:
text: use scale, proportion, and quantity to describe, compare, or model different systems;

subject: SCI
strand_text: Recurring themes and concepts. The student understands that recurring themes and concepts provide a framework for making connections across disciplines. The student is expected to:
text: examine and model the parts of a system and their interdependence in the function of the system;

subject: SCI
strand_text: Recurring themes and concepts. The student understands that recurring themes and concepts provide a framework for making connections across disciplines. The student is expected to:
text: investigate how energy flows and matter cycles through systems and how matter is conserved;

subject: SCI
strand_text: Recurring themes and concepts. The student understands that recurring themes and concepts provide a framework for making connections across disciplines. The student is expected to:
text: explain the relationship between the structure and function of objects, organisms, and systems; and

subject: SCI
strand_text: Recurring themes and concepts. The student understands that recurring themes and concepts provide a framework for making connections across disciplines. The student is expected to:
text: explain how factors or conditions impact stability and change in objects, organisms, and systems.

subject: SCI
strand_text: Matter and energy. The student knows that matter has measurable physical properties that determine how matter is identified, classified, changed, and used. The student is expected to:
text: classify and describe matter using observable physical properties, including temperature, mass, magnetism, relative density (the ability to sink or float in water), and physical state (solid, liquid, gas);

subject: SCI
strand_text: Matter and energy. The student knows that matter has measurable physical properties that determine how matter is identified, classified, changed, and used. The student is expected to:
text: investigate and compare a variety of mixtures, including solutions that are composed of liquids in liquids and solids in liquids; and

subject: SCI
strand_text: Matter and energy. The student knows that matter has measurable physical properties that determine how matter is identified, classified, changed, and used. The student is expected to:
text: demonstrate that matter is conserved when mixtures such as soil and water or oil and water are formed.

subject: SCI
strand_text: Force, motion, and energy. The student knows the nature of forces and the patterns of their interactions. The student is expected to plan and conduct descriptive investigations to explore the patterns of forces such as gravity, friction, or magnetism in contact or at a distance on an object.
text: Force, motion, and energy. The student knows the nature of forces and the patterns of their interactions. The student is expected to plan and conduct descriptive investigations to explore the patterns of forces such as gravity, friction, or magnetism in contact or at a distance on an object.

subject: SCI
strand_text: Force, motion, and energy. The student knows that energy is everywhere and can be observed in cycles, patterns, and systems. The student is expected to:
text: investigate and identify the transfer of energy by objects in motion, waves in water, and sound;

subject: SCI
strand_text: Force, motion, and energy. The student knows that energy is everywhere and can be observed in cycles, patterns, and systems. The student is expected to:
text: identify conductors and insulators of thermal and electrical energy; and

subject: SCI
strand_text: Force, motion, and energy. The student knows that energy is everywhere and can be observed in cycles, patterns, and systems. The student is expected to:
text: demonstrate and describe how electrical energy travels in a closed path that can produce light and thermal energy.

subject: SCI
strand_text: Earth and space. The student recognizes patterns among the Sun, Earth, and Moon system and their effects. The student is expected to:
text: collect and analyze data to identify sequences and predict patterns of change in seasons such as change in temperature and length of daylight; and

subject: SCI
strand_text: Earth and space. The student recognizes patterns among the Sun, Earth, and Moon system and their effects. The student is expected to:
text: collect and analyze data to identify sequences and predict patterns of change in the observable appearance of the Moon from Earth.

subject: SCI
strand_text: Earth and space. The student knows that there are processes on Earth that create patterns of change. The student is expected to:
text: describe and illustrate the continuous movement of water above and on the surface of Earth through the water cycle and explain the role of the Sun as a major source of energy in this process;

subject: SCI
strand_text: Earth and space. The student knows that there are processes on Earth that create patterns of change. The student is expected to:
text: model and describe slow changes to Earth's surface caused by weathering, erosion, and deposition from water, wind, and ice; and

subject: SCI
strand_text: Earth and space. The student knows that there are processes on Earth that create patterns of change. The student is expected to:
text: differentiate between weather and climate.

subject: SCI
strand_text: Earth and space. The student understands how natural resources are important and can be managed. The student is expected to:
text: identify and explain advantages and disadvantages of using Earth's renewable and nonrenewable natural resources such as wind, water, sunlight, plants, animals, coal, oil, and natural gas;

subject: SCI
strand_text: Earth and space. The student understands how natural resources are important and can be managed. The student is expected to:
text: explain the critical role of energy resources to modern life and how conservation, disposal, and recycling of natural resources impact the environment; and

subject: SCI
strand_text: Earth and space. The student understands how natural resources are important and can be managed. The student is expected to:
text: determine the physical properties of rocks that allow Earth's natural resources to be stored there.

subject: SCI
strand_text: Organisms and environments. The student describes patterns, cycles, systems, and relationships within environments. The student is expected to:
text: investigate and explain how most producers can make their own food using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide through the cycling of matter;

subject: SCI
strand_text: Organisms and environments. The student describes patterns, cycles, systems, and relationships within environments. The student is expected to:
text: describe the cycling of matter and flow of energy through food webs, including the roles of the Sun, producers, consumers, and decomposers; and

subject: SCI
strand_text: Organisms and environments. The student describes patterns, cycles, systems, and relationships within environments. The student is expected to:
text: identify and describe past environments based on fossil evidence, including common Texas fossils.

subject: SCI
strand_text: Organisms and environments. The student knows that organisms undergo similar life processes and have structures that function to help them survive within their environments. The student is expected to:
text: explore and explain how structures and functions of plants such as waxy leaves and deep roots enable them to survive in their environment; and

subject: SCI
strand_text: Organisms and environments. The student knows that organisms undergo similar life processes and have structures that function to help them survive within their environments. The student is expected to:
text: differentiate between inherited and acquired physical traits of organisms.

subject: SS
strand_text: History. The student understands the origins, similarities, and differences of American Indian groups in Texas before European exploration. The student is expected to:
text: explain the possible origins of American Indian groups in Texas;

subject: SS
strand_text: History. The student understands the origins, similarities, and differences of American Indian groups in Texas before European exploration. The student is expected to:
text: identify and compare the ways of life of American Indian groups in Texas before European exploration such as the Lipan Apache, Karankawa, Caddo, and Jumano;

subject: SS
strand_text: History. The student understands the origins, similarities, and differences of American Indian groups in Texas before European exploration. The student is expected to:
text: describe the cultural regions in which American Indians lived such as Gulf, Plains, Puebloan, and Southeastern; and

subject: SS
strand_text: History. The student understands the origins, similarities, and differences of American Indian groups in Texas before European exploration. The student is expected to:
text: locate American Indian groups remaining in Texas such as the Ysleta Del Sur Pueblo, Alabama-Coushatta, and Kickapoo.

subject: SS
strand_text: History. The student understands the causes and effects of European exploration and colonization of Texas. The student is expected to:
text: summarize motivations for European exploration and settlement of Texas, including economic opportunity, competition, and the desire for expansion;

subject: SS
strand_text: History. The student understands the causes and effects of European exploration and colonization of Texas. The student is expected to:
text: identify the accomplishments and explain the impact of significant explorers, including Cabeza de Vaca; Francisco Coronado; and René Robert Cavelier, Sieur de la Salle, on the settlement of Texas;

subject: SS
strand_text: History. The student understands the causes and effects of European exploration and colonization of Texas. The student is expected to:
text: explain when, where, and why the Spanish established settlements and Catholic missions in Texas as well as important individuals;

subject: SS
strand_text: History. The student understands the causes and effects of European exploration and colonization of Texas. The student is expected to:
text: identify Texas' role in the Mexican War of Independence and the war's impact on the development of Texas; and

subject: SS
strand_text: History. The student understands the causes and effects of European exploration and colonization of Texas. The student is expected to:
text: identify the accomplishments and explain the economic motivations and impact of significant empresarios, including Stephen F. Austin and Martín de León, on the settlement of Texas.

subject: SS
strand_text: History. The student understands the importance of the Texas Revolution, the Republic of Texas, and the annexation of Texas to the United States. The student is expected to:
text: analyze the causes, major events, and effects of the Texas Revolution, including the Battle of the Alamo, the Texas Declaration of Independence, the Runaway Scrape, and the Battle of San Jacinto;

subject: SS
strand_text: History. The student understands the importance of the Texas Revolution, the Republic of Texas, and the annexation of Texas to the United States. The student is expected to:
text: summarize the significant contributions of individuals such as William B. Travis, James Bowie, David Crockett, Juan N. Seguín, Plácido Benavides, José Francisco Ruiz, Antonio López de Santa Anna, Susanna Dickinson, and Enrique Esparza;

subject: SS
strand_text: History. The student understands the importance of the Texas Revolution, the Republic of Texas, and the annexation of Texas to the United States. The student is expected to:
text: identify leaders important to the founding of Texas as a republic and state, including José Antonio Navarro, Sam Houston, Mirabeau Lamar, and Anson Jones;

subject: SS
strand_text: History. The student understands the importance of the Texas Revolution, the Republic of Texas, and the annexation of Texas to the United States. The student is expected to:
text: describe the successes, problems, and organizations of the Republic of Texas such as the establishment of a constitution, economic struggles, relations with American Indians, and the Texas Rangers; and

subject: SS
strand_text: History. The student understands the importance of the Texas Revolution, the Republic of Texas, and the annexation of Texas to the United States. The student is expected to:
text: explain the events that led to the annexation of Texas to the United States and the impact of the U.S.-Mexican War.

subject: SS
strand_text: History. The student understands the political, economic, and social changes in Texas during the last half of the 19th century. The student is expected to:
text: describe the impact of the Civil War and Reconstruction on Texas;

subject: SS
